title: Plant Parts and Their Jobs
subject: Science
objectives: Students will be able to name and point to the roots, stem, leaves, and flower of a plant.
Students will be able to tell what roots and leaves do for a plant.
targets: I can name the parts of a plant.
I can tell what roots and leaves do.
materials: A real flowering plant (non-toxic, such as a geranium), and a weed pulled up with its roots
Wipes or the sink: hands get washed after touching soil
Sticky notes for the exit ticket

vocabulary.meaning: Grow under the ground. They soak up water and hold the plant still.
Holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
Uses light, air, and water to make food for the plant.
Makes seeds so new plants can grow.

sequence.teacher: Hold up the real plant. Ask the warm-up question; take three answers.

slides.title: Warm-up
slides.prompt: What does a plant need to grow?
slides.say: Write their answers on the board: water, sun, soil, air. We'll come back to them.

sequence.teacher: Name each part on the real plant as you show the labeled picture. Students point to the part on the real plant.
sequence.students: Point, repeat each word, and act out each job.

slides.title: Every part has a job

diagram.description: A simple plant with its parts labeled: flower, leaf, stem, roots.

slides.say: Point to each part on the real plant as you say it. Act it out: wiggle fingers down for roots, stand tall for the stem, arms out for leaves, hands in a cup for the flower. Leaves make food from light, air, and water.

slides.title: Plant words
slides.say: Read each word together. Point to it on the real plant.

slides.title: Quick check
slides.why: Roots grow in the soil, where the water is.
slides.say: One finger for A, two for B, three for C.

sequence.teacher: Ask what roots do and what leaves do before showing the slide; take answers, then show it. Ask: what would happen if a plant had no roots?
sequence.students: Say each job before it's shown.

slides.title: Two big jobs

left.heading: Roots
points: Hold the plant in the ground

slides.callout: No roots? The plant falls over and dries up.
slides.say: Point back to the warm-up list: water and sun are what roots and leaves need.

sequence.then: Done? Draw a plant on the back and label it.
sequence.teacher: Read each question aloud. Help with spelling only if asked; spelling doesn't count. Collect every sheet when time's up.
Hand out sticky notes. Students draw and write on their own, then stick the note on the door.
sequence.students: Draw and write on a sticky note.

slides.title: Exit ticket
slides.prompt: On your sticky note: draw a leaf. Write one thing it needs to make food.
slides.say: Notes that say soil or dirt: start there tomorrow. Soil gives water, but the leaves make the food.

checks: What would happen to a plant with no leaves?

misconceptions.misconception: Plants get their food from the soil.
misconceptions.response: Soil gives water. The leaves make food from light, air, and water.

misconceptions.misconception: The stem and the roots are the same part.
misconceptions.response: Show the ground line: the stem is above it, the roots are below it.

support: Let students use the word bank and point instead of write.
Pair students to read the questions together.
extension: Find a part of a plant we eat (carrot: root, lettuce: leaf).
language: Point to each part on the labeled picture and say its name together.
Accept answers drawn or said in the student's first language, then name the English word together.

walkthrough.think: Which part grows under the ground?
walkthrough.idea: Each part has its place: the flower on top, the roots under the ground.
steps: Top: the flower. Under the ground: the roots.
The leaves grow out of the stem.
mistakes: Mixing up the stem and the roots.

walkthrough.think: Where do the roots grow, and what's there?
walkthrough.idea: Roots soak up water and hold the plant in the ground.
walkthrough.model: The roots soak up water from the soil. They hold the plant in the ground.
mistakes: Saying roots make food. The leaves do that.

walkthrough.think: Where does a plant make its food, and what does that part need?
walkthrough.idea: Leaves use light, with air and water, to make food.
steps: Plants make food in their leaves.
Leaves need light to do it.
mistakes: Picking soil: soil gives water, but the leaves make the food.

assessment: A student who has it names and points to all four parts and says what roots and leaves do: roots take in water and hold the plant, leaves make food using light.
